before: Forty days have passed since the birth from the virgin, and [the Child] has now come into earthly Jerusalem. Concerning this child, Habakkuk proclaimed, saying: 'God will come from Teman,' that is, from the south (Habakkuk 3:3). For from the south of Jerusalem, from Bethlehem, He has now come into Zion. Because of this, the child was testified to you by Moses, saying that the Lord God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, and every one not listening to him, his soul shall be destroyed (Deuteronomy 18:15, 19; cf. Acts 3:23).

Concerning this child, the prophet David prayed, saying: 'He who sits upon the cherubim, appear; stir up your power and come to save us' (Psalms 99:1; 79:3). And again: 'Let your mercies hasten to us, O Lord' (Psalm 78:8). And again: 'Lord, bend your heavens and come down' (Psalm 143:5). And in another way: 'You, Lord God of powers, attend to visit all the nations. Therefore know, O nations, and be humbled' (Isaiah 8:9).

Behold, Jews, and be persuaded: this child angels hymn, archangels worship, powers tremble at, powers glorify, cherubim serve, and seraphim theologize about. To him the sun serves, to him the moon ministers, to him the elements obey, and to him the springs are subject.
Seeing this child, the gates of Hades were crushed, and the heavenly gates were opened, and Hades, seeing, was terrified.

This child abolished death, shamed the devil, loosed the curse, stopped sorrow, crushed the serpent, cut the middle partition, tore through the evil handwriting of sins, trampled sin, destroyed error, and raised creation. This child saved Adam, remade Eve, called the nations, and enlightened the world.

Therefore, come you also, lovers of Christ and lovers of God. Let us all meet the Lord and Master brightly and purely, not legally, but spiritually; not feasting with the stomach, but leaping with the spirit; not drinking wine, but burning with the Spirit. In this way, let us today brightly adorn the lamps.

In this way, as children of light, let us bring the candles to the true Light, Christ, because he shone as a light unto revelation of the nations to the world. Therefore, as lights from light, let us rise up above the snow, having been hardened above milk, having been polished above sapphire stone, and having flown like white doves into the heavens, so let us emerge into the meeting with God in the clouds.

Let us all today and forever shout the things of the feast. Let us dance with angels. Let us shine with shepherds. Let us worship with the magi. Let us celebrate with Bethlehem. Let us meet with Zion. Let us be sanctified with the temple. Let us rejoice, magnifying the Virgin. Let us present ourselves with Joseph, like two fruits, the soul and the body. Let us embrace Christ with Simeon, and let us confess with Anna. So that we may be found within the eternal good things by the grace and mercies and philanthropy of the Lord and God and Savior of us, Jesus Christ, to whom belongs the glory and the power with the Father and the Holy Spirit unto the ages of ages. Amen.

before: Separating [himself], this is the treasure of the paternal goodness and everlasting blessedness. This is the water of life and the life being granted to the world. This is the uncreated ray, being born from the fore-light of the sun, but not being cut.

This is the God-Logos, having composed all things into being by word alone from non-being into being. This is the Phosphoros, having arranged the incorporeal powers of the heavenly, incorporeal, invisible hosts and ranks before the Phosphoros. This is the one who stretched out the heaven alone and walks upon the sea as if upon dry land. This is the one who shrouded the abyss with mist. This is the one who made the earth firm upon the waters. This is the one who enclosed the sea with sand. This is the one who distinguished the light from the darkness. This is the one who arranged the circular ornamentation of the stars. This is the one who composed the whole visible and intelligible cosmos in wisdom.

This is the one who, with unhandy hands, fashioned and shaped man from clay. This is the one who created us according to the image of God, and now himself, according to the image, having become man. Man, but indeed also the same God.

Man is the visible, entirely as I myself am with them, so that having cleansed me he might save me; God is the intelligible, possessing the essence from a perfect and perfect Father. He, existing in the form of God, has now taken my form in a masterly way as a slave, not diminishing the dignity of divinity, but sanctifying the essence of my nature.

Wholly above and wholly below, the same being known, having been born above without time and below without seed; a maker of the things above as God and a creature of the things below as man. Listen to these things, all you nations; listen, O Israel. The Lord your God, this is He, whom I, your priest Simeon, bearing in my arms, proclaim with a great voice, testifying to the people in the temple. Therefore pay attention, my people, to my word; incline the ear of you to the words of my mouth.

This child is the one about whom Isaiah proclaimed, saying, 'A child is born to us, a son is given to us, and his name is called, of great counsel (of the Father), Angel, Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Ruler, O Israel, Prince of Peace, Father of the age to come' (Isaiah 9:6). If then this child is a Mighty God, it is evident concerning Him that David said, 'The God of gods shall be seen in Zion' (Psalm 89:12). Concerning this child Jeremiah cries out: 'That God appeared upon the earth and with men walked' (Jeremiah 24:7).
